findings.title: No-auth Responses success fixture omits a backend-required model
findings.trigger: Run the test named can explicitly configure a Responses service without authentication. The read fixture omits model; the only interaction clears the API key and submits the form.

evidence.detail: mutate is unconditionally resolved; the provider fixture at 109-114 has no model.
The test only toggles no API key and clicks save; its assertion at 126 checks only apiKey and allowInsecureHttp.
Missing model becomes the empty form value.

Empty model is omitted from the system/provider/write parameters. The constructed parameters are expectedRevision r, kind responses, baseUrl http://192.168.1.5/v1, allowInsecureHttp false, apiKey empty.
Root management forwards the same parameters to provider/write.
Responses requires small_text(params.get("model"), "model"); small_text at 41-43 rejects missing/empty values with Invalid model.

findings.impact: The test passes on a payload the deployed validator rejects, so this named success case cannot detect loss of the required model field. This is a test-validity gap, not evidence that a correctly populated no-auth Responses configuration is unusable.
findings.recommendation: Supply a valid model in the read fixture or enter it through the form, and assert the valid complete write parameters including model. Keep a missing-model rejection test separate if desired.
findings.verification: Confirmed by current test-to-form-to-manager static control flow; no production service or live provider invocation.

limitations: Static audit only: neither focused Vitest execution nor the full suite was run during this supplemental review.
No real browser WebRTC/microphone, native PTY, external MCP, provider inference, remote sharing/upload, production deployment or personal credentials were used.
Jsdom component tests and local substitutes do not establish real-browser media/terminal behavior, deployed service integration, or public HTTPS reachability.
Supporting implementation files were cross-read at relevant control-flow sections; only the 23 assigned test files are counted as complete full-file review coverage.
